newsitem.title: USA: FUND VIEW - Delaware Real Estate cautions on returns.
newsitem.headline: FUND VIEW - Delaware Real Estate cautions on returns.

text.p: A word of caution from Babak Zenouzi, portfolio manager of the Delaware Pooled Real Estate Investment Trust Portfolio: Don't expect the same huge returns that the mutual fund has booked over the last year.
The fund has gained 48.02 percent in the last 12 months through last Friday, making it the top performer in the sector, according to Lipper Analytical Services.
Since the fund came out of the gate in December 1995, it has returned 57.03 percent, placing third among about 50 funds.

"Those returns are not sustainable for REITS," Zenouzi said. "REIT investors should expect a low-to-mid teen type of return." But if you combine dividend yields of as much as six percent, and cash flow growth at nine percent, REITs are still nifty investments, Zenouzi said.
He attributed the big gains over the last 12 months to some good bets in the multi-family apartment and hotel REITs.

Some successful performers over the last 12 months include apartment REITs Ambassador Apartment Inc, which has risen to 25-3/8 from 18 last March, and Equity Residential Properties Trust, up to 47-1/2 from 31 a year ago.
Among hotel REITs, Patriot American Hospitality Inc has risen to 24-1/2 from 14-1/4, and Starwood Lodging Trust jumped to 44-1/2 from 22.
Patriot is the top holding in the fund at about 3.90 percent of the portfolio, while Starwood comprises 3.10 percent and holds the number five spot.
Zenouzi traces the moves of Patriot and Starwood to a cap on the supply of full-service hotels, the low cost of working capital, and strong management teams.
Zenouzi said REITs generally have been able to acquire many properties at below replacement cost, employed strong management, and improved occupancy rates and raised rents.
"The fundamental are very strong in the whole real estate industry," said Zenouzi. "There's also the acceptance of the REIT vehicle."

He said a lot of new money has been investing in the REIT sector, especially by managers of balanced and equity income mutual funds. As the REIT sector has risen to comprise about eight percent of the Russell 2000 small-cap index, "a lot of managers have had to make a bet," he said.

Zenouzi still likes the apartment -- or multi-family -- sector, especially in California. "The zoning is difficult in California," he said. "There are fewer being built; there's a lid on supply." The sector comprises 16 percent of the fund.

He is also bullish on the office industrial group, which is the biggest sector at about 32 percent. "There's a lack of supply coming on line," he said. "Occupancies are high, and there are nice rent rises."
Zenouzi said REITs were long viewed as bland securities with inherent conflicts of interest, as managers profited no matter how the REITS performed.
Zenouzi said REITs have undergone some fundamental changes to help improve their image.
REITs are now self-managed and fully integrated operating companies, and have virtually the same governance framework as more traditional companies, he said.
He also cited the high rate of stock ownership by management and employees -- 16 percent on average.
Other top holdings in the $50 million fund include Vornado Realty Trust at 3.50 percent; Simon DeBartolo Group Inc at 3.45 percent; and Kilroy Realty Corp at 3.26 percent.
